sd_custer_state_park.blurb: This corner of the Black Hills holds the Needles, a landscape of eroded granite pillars, towers and spires. Trad climbing leads, with a solid sport contingent, some bouldering and a little ice. The signature style is bold face climbing on quartz-crystal holds, alongside crack climbing, in routes of one to four pitches. Grades start at the easy fives and reach 5.13, with the bulk between 5.7 and 5.11. Sylvan Lake is by far the biggest zone, followed by the Cathedral Spires, home to many multi-pitch trad lines, the Needles Eye area and Tenpins/Switchbacks. The rock is granite, and the climbing season runs from spring to fall.

id_city_of_rocks.blurb: City of Rocks is a field of granite formations in rural southern Idaho, close to the Utah line and around 6,500 feet up. The granite is varnished and pocketed: where the dark coating wears through, the exposed stone erodes into edges and pockets. Trad leads, with a large sport selection, some top-rope and a good bouldering area. Climbs range from about 30 to 600 feet, with grades from 5.4 to 5.13 and the heart of the range at 5.8 to 5.11. Breadloaves is the biggest formation, followed by Graham Creek and Bath Rock. Protection can be mixed, and a bolted line may peter out partway up, so bring gear to back up sport-looking routes.

bc_sea_to_sky_squamish_to_whistler.blurb: A string of crags along the highway between Squamish and Whistler, with Cheakamus Canyon the biggest hub and Area 44, Cal-Cheak and Nordic Rock adding more. Nearly everything is sport. Most lines are 5.10 to 5.12, with a fair number of moderates around 5.9 and a handful of hard ones into the 5.13s and 5.14s. The granite is smoother and more compact than the rock of the Chief near Squamish, which favours hard, smooth face climbing and rarely suits trad. Expect vertical to overhanging terrain: crimpy faces, big roofs, endurance lines and short power routes. Some of the overhanging, sheltered crags can be climbed on rainy days.

ca_big_bear_city_area.blurb: This area covers the crags north and east of Big Bear City in the San Bernardino Mountains, around 7,200 feet. Holcomb Valley Pinnacles dominates, with North Shore Boulders, Tanglewood Slabs and Jacoby Canyon adding more. Bouldering and sport are close to level, followed by trad and some top-rope. Most roped climbs run from 5.6 to 5.11, with 5.10 the biggest group, and most Pinnacles routes are 5.10 or easier. The Pinnacles sit among pines just north of Big Bear Lake, on granite that is mostly good, where steep-looking lines often go at moderate grades thanks to the holds. Climbing is possible year-round depending on the winter; summers get hot, so shade is valued, and early and late seasons tend to be quieter.

ut_northeast_utah.blurb: A broad region stretching from the south slope of the Uinta Mountains to the canyons around Vernal and the Flaming Gorge country. The Uintas hold most of the climbing: steep quartzite with horizontal cracks, at high elevation, away from valley summer heat, with sport and trad as well as alpine routes and some ice. The Vernal area is desert sandstone adventure climbing, where the rock can be loose and soft. Around Flaming Gorge, bouldering is the most developed, along with some sport and trad, mostly on sandstone. Roped grades mostly fall between 5.8 and 5.11, with a few harder lines into the 5.12s, and the ice and mixed climbing adds a winter side.

co_st_vrain_canyons.blurb: Three canyons west of Lyons, cut by the South, Middle and North forks of the St. Vrain River. The South Fork holds the great majority of the climbing, the North Fork is a distant second, and the Middle Fork is small. Trad leads, with a good amount of sport and some bouldering. The rock is granite, mostly good quality though some is coarse or chossy. Older routes follow crack systems and newer sport lines go up faces and steep roofs. Most climbs are short, up to about five pitches, and grades mostly fall from 5.7 to 5.11, with a smaller number of harder lines. The rock faces every direction, so climbing is possible year-round, with summer and fall best.
